explanations: Yes. Links are filtered with a denylist of two schemes matched at the very start of the raw string. Anything else that contains a colon is stored as-is: data:text/html,..., a leading space or tab before javascript: (browsers strip leading whitespace in href), or a scheme split by an embedded tab or newline like java\tscript:. The renderer HTML-escapes the attribute, but escaping does not neutralise a dangerous URL scheme, so clicking the link runs script. Links should be parsed with URL and accepted only if the protocol is on an allowlist (http:/https:).

The raw value has no colon, so https:// is prepended; new URL parses it and the hostname example.com becomes the label. It is not rejected, the href is rewritten rather than kept raw, and the code uses https, not http.

PostService only trims, NFC-normalises and length-checks the body; it stores the original text. renderPostCard passes it through esc, so < and > become entities and nothing executes. There is no rejection and no stripping at write time.

The MAX_LINKS check runs before the loop over links, so 5 links fail immediately with 'at most 4 links per post'. The per-link check is never reached, and nothing is stored, because validation throws before repo.insert.
